key_insight: CFG-Ctrl reframes Classifier-Free Guidance as a control signal applied to a continuous-time generative flow: the conditional–unconditional discrepancy is used as an error to adjust the model's velocity field, showing vanilla CFG is effectively a proportional (P) controller with fixed gain.
problem_solved: Clarifies and unifies why CFG modifies diffusion trajectories to improve semantic alignment, enabling principled analysis and more systematic design of guidance mechanisms for flow-based diffusion models.
method: Reinterpret CFG within a control-theoretic framework on first-order continuous-time generative flows.
Use the conditional–unconditional output discrepancy as an error signal to compute a corrective control that modifies the velocity field during generation.
Characterize standard CFG as a proportional controller (P-control) with fixed gain, paving the way for alternative controller designs and tunable guidance.
impact: Provides a principled perspective that helps practitioners reason about and tune guidance strength, design more stable or adaptive guidance strategies, and bridge diffusion guidance with classical control tools for improved semantic alignment.
visual_elements: Control-loop diagram showing unconditional flow, conditional flow, discrepancy (error) calculation, and the control signal applied to the velocity field.
Simple block diagram labeling vanilla CFG as a P-controller with fixed gain versus a generic controller block for CFG-Ctrl extensions.
Trajectory visualization of sample paths with and without CFG-Ctrl illustrating improved semantic alignment.
Chart showing guidance strength (gain) vs alignment/quality trade-off to convey tuning effects.
paper_authors: Hanyang Wang, Yiyang Liu, Jiawei Chi, Fangfu Liu, Ran Xue
